Barcode Count Example¶

This example counts items with a USB barcode scanner. Each item carries a 2D barcode, and every scan becomes one test result, so Lente counts the items, by product and lot.

The example is in public/prism/scripts/example/barcode_count_v0,

  • count_0.scr - the script

  • tst00xx.py - the test program

  • make_barcodes.py - makes a PDF sheet of QR codes to print

  • barcodes_P001.pdf - a sample sheet

The driver is public/prism/drivers/scanners.

Barcode Format¶

The barcode holds P###-S#####, where P### is the product model number and ##### is the product serial number, for example P001-S00123.

The test checks each scan against the regex in the script, TST000_Scan args regex, ^(?P<product>Pd{3})-S(?P<sn>d{5})$. The regex groups product and sn pick the fields from the barcode, so a different barcode format only needs a new regex,

  • product is saved as the result info product, P001

  • sn is saved as key0, sn:00123

  • the whole barcode is saved as the measurement TST000_Scan.barcode

A scan that does not match the format is recorded as a FAIL.

Make a sheet of barcodes to print with,

cd public/prism/scripts/example/barcode_count_v0
python make_barcodes.py --product P001 --start 123 --count 24

This writes barcodes_P001.pdf, 12 codes per Letter page.

Lot¶

The Lot is entered when the script is loaded, in the format YYYYMMDD-##, a date and a two digit number, for example 20261025-01 for the first lot of the day. It is saved as the result info lot, and Lente can show yield and counts by lot.

Scanner¶

The scanner must be in USB keyboard mode (HID), the usual factory setting. The scanner “types” the barcode followed by Enter, into the Prism text box.

  • The Prism Test Portal page must have the keyboard focus when scanning

  • The driver finds the scanner by its USB manufacturer, see SCANNER_MANUFACTURERS in hwdrv_scanners.py. Datalogic is supported, add your scanner’s manufacturer as required. python public/prism/drivers/scanners/hwdrv_scanners.py lists the scanners found.

  • If no scanner is found, the script does not load

  • A scanner in keyboard mode cannot be told apart from another scanner, or from the keyboard, so there is only one channel, even with more scanners attached.

Running¶

After the script is loaded and started, the operator just keeps scanning. The scanner driver restarts the script after each scan, there is no button to press.

The scan item has a 5 minute timeout (“timeout”: 300 in the script). If nothing is scanned in that time, the item is recorded as TIMEOUT and the script stops restarting, so an idle station sends one TIMEOUT result, not one every 5 minutes. To resume, press the channel number (Start) button on the Test Portal, and the next good scan turns the automatic restarts back on.

Change the timeout to suit, see Timeouts and Aborts.

Command Line Testing¶

The script runs with prism_dev.py (see Development), the barcode is scanned into the terminal prompt,

python prism_dev.py --script public/prism/scripts/example/barcode_count_v0/count_0.scr

prism_dev.py runs the script once, and the result file is written to the current folder.

Script¶

// Example: Count barcoded items with a USB barcode scanner (keyboard mode)
//          Barcode string looks like: P###-S#####, P### product, ##### serial number
//          The regex groups "product" and "sn" pick the fields from the barcode,
//          info:product is filled in from the barcode, dB key0 is the serial number
//          The script restarts after each scan, if no scan within the item timeout,
//          the item records TIMEOUT and the restarts stop, press channel Start to resume.
//          Make barcodes with make_barcodes.py, see sample barcodes_P001.pdf
{
  "subs": {
    "Lot": {
      "title": "Lot (format YYYYMMDD-##)",
      "type" : "str", "widget": "textinput",
      "regex": "^20\\d{2}(0[1-9]|1[0-2])(0[1-9]|[12]\\d|3[01])-\\d{2}$",
      "default": "20261025-01"
    },
    "Loc": {
      "title": "Location",
      "type" : "str", "widget": "select", "choices": ["canada/ontario/milton",
                                                      "us/newyork/buffalo"]
    }
  },
  "info": {
    "product": "N/A",
    "bom": "N/A",
    "lot": "%%Lot",
    "location": "%%Loc"
  },
  "config": {
    "fail_fast": true,
    "drivers": ["public.prism.drivers.scanners.hwdrv_scanners"]
  },
  "tests": [
    {
      "module": "public.prism.scripts.example.barcode_count_v0.tst00xx",
      "options": { "fail_fast": false },
      "items": [
        {"id": "TST000_Scan",           "enable": true, "timeout": 300,
                                        "args": {"regex": "^(?P<product>P\\d{3})-S(?P<sn>\\d{5})$"} },
        {"id": "TST0xxTEARDOWN",        "enable": true }
      ]
    }
  ]
}

Program¶

#! /usr/bin/env python
# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""
Sistemi Corporation, copyright, all rights reserved, 2026
Martin Guthrie

"""
import re
import logging
from core.test_item import TestItem
from public.prism.api import ResultAPI

from public.prism.drivers.scanners.Scanners import DRIVER_TYPE as DRIVER_TYPE_SCANNER


# file and class name must match
class tst00xx(TestItem):

    # The item timeout ends the textbox wait, so this only has to be longer than any item timeout
    TEXTBOX_TIMEOUT_SEC = 24 * 60 * 60

    def __init__(self, controller, chan, shared_state):
        super().__init__(controller, chan, shared_state)
        self.logger = logging.getLogger("tst00xx.{}".format(self.chan))

    def _scanner(self):
        """ The scanner driver for this channel, or None """
        drivers = self.shared_state.get_drivers(self.chan, type=DRIVER_TYPE_SCANNER)
        if not drivers: return None
        return drivers[0]["obj"]["hwdrv"]

    def TST0xxTEARDOWN(self):
        """  Always called at the end of testing
        - process any cleanup, closing, etc

            {"id": "TST0xxTEARDOWN",        "enable": true },

        """
        ctx = self.item_start()  # always first line of test
        self.item_end()  # always last line of test

    def TST000_Scan(self):
        """ Scan barcode
        - args.regex is the barcode format, P###-S#####, its groups "product" and "sn"
          pick the fields, product goes to info product, sn is the serial number key
        - if nothing is scanned before the item timeout, Prism records TIMEOUT,
          and the scanner stops restarting the script, until the next good scan

        {"id": "TST000_Scan", "enable": true, "timeout": 300,
                              "args": {"regex": "^(?P<product>P\\d{3})-S(?P<sn>\\d{5})$"} },

        """
        ctx = self.item_start()   # always first line of test
        scanner = self._scanner()

        self.log_bullet("Scan barcode")
        user_text = self.input_textbox("Scan:", "barcode", timeout=self.TEXTBOX_TIMEOUT_SEC)

        if not user_text["success"]:
            # timed out or aborted, stop restarting the script, Prism records the TIMEOUT
            if scanner: scanner.stop_player()
            self.log_bullet("No scan: {}".format(user_text.get("err")))
            self.log_bullet("Press channel Start to resume")
            self.item_end(ResultAPI.RECORD_RESULT_FAIL)
            return

        barcode = user_text["textbox"].strip()
        match = re.match(ctx.item.args.regex, barcode)
        if not match:
            _, _result, _bullet = ctx.record.measurement("barcode", barcode, ResultAPI.UNIT_STRING,
                                                         force_fail=True)
            self.log_bullet("Bad format: {}".format(barcode))
            self.item_end(_result)
            return

        ctx.record.record_info_set({"product": match.group("product")})
        ctx.record.add_key("sn", match.group("sn"), slot=0)

        # Note: ResultAPI.UNIT_STRING is used to format the measurement correctly in JSON
        _, _result, _bullet = ctx.record.measurement("barcode", barcode, ResultAPI.UNIT_STRING)
        self.log_bullet(_bullet)

        # a good scan (re)starts the automatic restarts, after a timeout and channel Start
        if scanner: scanner.start_player()

        self.item_end(_result)  # always last line of test
